readings.title: Counting shade instead of trunks
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A housing estate proudly reported that it had planted eighty trees. Residents still complained that the main walking route was hot and exposed. The landscape team mapped where people walked at midday and where existing trees cast shade. Many new trees stood on an unused grass strip far from the route. The team did not remove them, but it placed future planting beside heavily used paths where space allowed. It also explained that young trees would take time to provide substantial cover. Counting trunks described an activity; mapping useful shade brought the estate closer to understanding the benefit residents were seeking.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The bench under discussion
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When a park proposed moving a bench closer to a tree, a drawing made the change look simple. Consultation revealed competing needs. Older walkers liked the shade, while wheelchair users noted that the ground beneath the tree was uneven. Maintenance staff needed room to inspect the trunk. The final layout put the bench near the shade edge on a firm surface, leaving a clear space beside it and access behind it. No participant received the first arrangement they imagined, but each could identify a need that had shaped the result. The discussion improved the design by making hidden requirements visible.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

questions.explanation: 把隐藏需求显现出来以形成综合设计。

readings.title: The photograph taken in winter
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A resident posted a winter photograph of a street and claimed that its trees provided almost no shade. A gardening club used the image in a lesson about evidence. The photograph accurately showed bare branches on that date, but it could not establish conditions throughout the year. Members took additional photographs from the same point in spring and summer and recorded the time of day. The series revealed changes that a single image could not show. The club did not dismiss the original photograph as false. It distinguished a valid observation from a claim that extended beyond the observation's scope.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

questions.explanation: 照片被用来声称树木几乎不遮阴。

readings.title: A planting day with a second date
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A company sponsored a neighbourhood planting day and invited employees for photographs. The community gardener welcomed the help but asked the organisers to set another date six weeks later. On the return visit, volunteers checked labels, cleared competing growth around young plants and recorded losses for the gardener to assess. Fewer people attended the second event, but those who came understood why the original celebration was only a beginning. The company subsequently funded a season of maintenance rather than another large opening event. The gardener valued enthusiasm most when it developed into dependable care over time.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

A tree planted today becomes part of a place that will continue to change. Its future size, the needs of nearby residents and the work required to care for it all deserve attention. A successful planting programme therefore looks beyond the number planted on one occasion. It asks whether living trees will remain useful and well supported over many years.
translation.referenceAnswer: 今天种下的一棵树，会成为一个持续变化的地方的一部分。它未来的体量、附近居民的需求和照料它所需的工作，都值得关注。因此，成功的种植计划不会只看某次种下的数量，而会思考这些活树在多年后是否仍有用，并得到妥善支持。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Your neighbourhood has funding for trees and seating near a walking route. Write a proposal explaining how to choose locations, consult users and organise continuing care.
writing.sampleAnswer: I suggest that we first observe where people walk and rest during different parts of the day. This will help identify places where shade and seating would be useful. Before selecting trees, a qualified planner should consider their mature size and underground services. Residents should comment on a simple layout, especially people who use wheelchairs or walking aids. Seats need firm ground and enough clear space around them. We should also name a maintenance coordinator and reserve part of the funding for continuing care. A planting day can bring neighbours together, but progress should be reported through later visits as well. The aim is a comfortable route that remains useful after the opening celebration.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。

criteria.description: 用词准确，句式基本正确；根据错误对表达和理解的影响扣分。
